unit.why: A quoted homiletic passage from Avodat Yisrael that holds two brief exemplary anecdotes: one about the Ari and one about R. Yehiel Michel, each revealing a man's hidden sin, followed by a moral exhortation to shame and repentance.
unit.boundary_note: Both anecdotes sit inside a homiletic frame (quotation from עבודת ישראל ending with an ethical call); they could arguably be classed as saying_or_teaching.

stories.start_quote: כמעשה האר״י ז״ל שאמר לאדם א׳
stories.end_quote: והציב לפניו העבירה עצמה שעבר עלי׳
stories.summary_en: The Ari told a man all the sins he had committed. The man admitted all but one, so the Ari passed his hand over the man's face and made the sin itself appear before him.

tags.why: Wonder of the Ari, a pre-Hasidic kabbalist
Cited as an example inside a homiletic discourse on tzaddikim who recognize sins
